target_pattern: Use tener + noun chunks for personal states and age, use tener ganas de + infinitive for desire, use hacer for ambient weather temperature, and use estar + adjective for object temperature and spiciness.

cognitive_shift.english_trap: Overusing estar for states that Spanish packages with tener.
cognitive_shift.spanish_logic: High-frequency personal states are expressed as possession chunks in Spanish, while weather and object temperature use different verbs.
target_pattern_formula: tener + noun chunk for personal state
tener ganas de + infinitive for desire
estar + adjective for object temperature and picante
natural_examples: Tengo mucha hambre despues del trabajo.
Tenemos ganas de salir esta noche.

controlled_recombination.instructions: Write each in Spanish using the target pattern.
prompts_en: Do you feel like going out tonight?

pattern_mutation.instructions: Transform each base sentence as instructed.
drills: Base: Tengo hambre. -> intensify with mucha.
Base: Tenemos sed. -> change subject to yo.
Base: Tengo frio. -> change to plural subject ellos and intensify.
Base: Hace calor. -> change to cold and add hoy.
Base: El cafe esta caliente. -> intensify correctly.
Base: La comida esta picante. -> change to very spicy.
Base: Tengo 30 anos. -> change age to 54.
Base: Juan tiene 20 anos. -> make a yes/no question.
Base: Tengo ganas de ir a la playa. -> change infinitive to comer.
Base: Tienes ganas de salir? -> change subject to ustedes.
Base: Tengo prisa. -> make it negative.
Base: Tengo suerte. -> change subject to nosotros.
Base: Tengo la culpa. -> change to tu and negative.
Base: El cuarto esta caliente. -> change to weather sentence with hacer.

prompts: I am hungry. (Tengo hambre. vs Estoy hambre.)
I am very thirsty. (Tengo mucha sed. vs Tengo muy sed.)
I am cold, feeling. (Tengo frio. vs Estoy frio.)
It is hot today. (Hace calor hoy. vs Esta caliente hoy.)
The coffee is very hot. (El cafe esta muy caliente. vs El cafe tiene mucho calor.)
I am 30 years old. (Tengo 30 anos. vs Soy 30 anos.)
I feel like going out. (Tengo ganas de salir. vs Estoy ganas de salir.)
I am sleepy. (Tengo sueno. vs Estoy sueno.)
I am in a hurry. (Tengo prisa. vs Estoy prisa.)
The eagle is thirsty. (El aguila tiene sed. vs La aguila tiene sed.)

guided_personal_writing.instructions: Write one Spanish sentence for each specific meaning.
prompts: Write that you are very hungry after your workout.
Write that your team is thirsty after a long meeting.
Write that you are 35 years old.
Write that your father is 68 years old.
Write that you feel like staying home tonight.
Write that you ask a friend if they feel like getting coffee.
Write that you are very sleepy this morning.
Write that you are in a hurry because you have a call in five minutes.
Write that it is very hot in your city today.
Write that your office is cold.
Write that your coffee is too hot right now.
Write that your lunch is spicy but good.
Write that your project team is lucky.
Write that it is not your coworker s fault.
Write that you have to leave because you are in a hurry.

reverse_conceptual_expression.instructions: Write natural Spanish, not literal English.
prompts_en: I am really thirsty right now.
We are hungry but we cannot eat yet.
Do you feel like watching a movie?
It is very hot today, but the office is cold.
I am sleepy, I need coffee.

common_errors.why_it_happens: Using adjective intensifier with noun chunk.

common_errors.mistake: Estoy frio for personal sensation in this lesson pattern
Tengo 30 without anos in beginner production

common_errors.why_it_happens: Ignoring stressed a feminine noun article rule.
common_errors.correct_spanish: El aguila in singular, las aguilas in plural.

reverse_conceptual_expression: Tenemos hambre pero no podemos comer todavia.
Tienes ganas de ver una pelicula?
